name: UNKNOWN
title: Unknown Protocol
description: Traffic that nDPI couldn't match to any known protocol. Could be custom software, obfuscated traffic, or a protocol not yet in the database.

name: FTP_CONTROL
title: File Transfer Protocol – Control
description: The command channel for FTP. Your computer sends instructions here like 'list files' or 'download this file'. Think of it as the remote control for moving files between computers.

name: MAIL_POP
title: Post Office Protocol (POP3)
description: An older email pickup protocol. Your email app connects to the mail server, downloads your messages, and (usually) deletes them from the server — like picking up physical mail from a post office.

name: MAIL_SMTP
title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
description: The universal protocol for sending email. Every time you hit 'Send', SMTP carries your message from your device to your email provider's server, and from server to server until it reaches the recipient.

name: MAIL_IMAP
title: Internet Message Access Protocol
description: Modern email sync protocol. Unlike POP3, IMAP keeps your emails on the server and syncs them across all your devices — so reading email on your phone also marks it read on your laptop.

name: DNS
title: Domain Name System
description: The internet's phonebook. When you type 'google.com', DNS translates that human-readable name into a numeric IP address your computer can actually connect to. Nearly every internet connection starts with a DNS lookup.

name: IPP
title: Internet Printing Protocol
description: Lets you send print jobs to a networked printer. When you print a document over Wi-Fi, IPP carries the job from your computer to the printer.

name: HTTP
title: Hypertext Transfer Protocol
description: The foundation of the web. Every time you visit a website, HTTP (or its secure cousin HTTPS) is what your browser uses to request pages and receive content back from web servers.

name: MDNS
title: Multicast DNS
description: Lets devices on your local network find each other by name without needing a central DNS server. This is how your Mac discovers an Apple TV or a printer on the same Wi-Fi network.

name: NTP
title: Network Time Protocol
description: Keeps your computer's clock accurate by syncing it with internet time servers. Without NTP, your computer's clock would drift and things like security certificates and scheduled tasks would break.

name: NETBIOS
title: Network Basic I/O System
description: An older Windows networking protocol for sharing files and printers on local networks. Modern Windows uses SMB instead, but NetBIOS name resolution is still common on older networks.

name: NFS
title: Network File System
description: Lets you mount and access files on a remote server as if they were local files on your computer. Very common in Linux/Unix enterprise environments for shared storage.

name: SSDP
title: Simple Service Discovery Protocol
description: Allows devices on your network to automatically announce and discover each other's services. Used by smart TVs, Chromecast, Xbox, and other UPnP devices to make themselves visible on your network.

name: BGP
title: Border Gateway Protocol
description: The protocol that holds the internet together. BGP is how different internet providers (ISPs) exchange routing information to agree on how to send packets across the globe. It's only used between large networks.

name: SNMP
title: Simple Network Management Protocol
description: Used by network engineers to remotely monitor and manage routers, switches, and servers. It can query device stats like CPU usage, interface traffic, and hardware temperature.

name: XDMCP
title: X Display Manager Control Protocol
description: Allows remote graphical login sessions on Linux/Unix systems — essentially remote desktop for older Unix systems. Less common today, replaced by VNC and RDP.

name: SMBV1
title: Server Message Block v1
description: The original Windows file-sharing protocol. SMBv1 is notoriously insecure and was exploited by the WannaCry ransomware. Microsoft and security experts strongly recommend disabling it.
note: ⚠️ Security risk — SMBv1 was exploited by the WannaCry ransomware. Disable if detected.

name: SYSLOG
title: System Log Protocol
description: A standardized way for network devices (routers, switches, firewalls) and servers to send log messages to a central logging server. Crucial for monitoring and incident response.

name: DHCP
title: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
description: Automatically assigns IP addresses to devices joining a network. When you connect to Wi-Fi, DHCP is what gives your device its IP address, subnet mask, gateway, and DNS server — all within milliseconds.

name: POSTGRES
title: PostgreSQL Database Protocol
description: Network traffic to/from a PostgreSQL database server. Postgres is an advanced open-source database used by many web applications and data platforms.

name: MYSQL
title: MySQL Database Protocol
description: Network traffic to/from a MySQL database server. MySQL is one of the most popular databases in the world, powering countless websites and applications.

name: MS_OUTLOOK
title: Microsoft Outlook
description: Traffic from the Microsoft Outlook email client communicating with Exchange or Microsoft 365 servers. Includes email sync, calendar, contacts, and task management.

name: VK
title: VKontakte (VK)
description: Russia's largest social network, similar to Facebook. VK is popular across Eastern Europe and Russia for social networking, messaging, and media sharing.

name: MAIL_POPS
title: POP3 Secure (POP3S)
description: The encrypted version of POP3 — same email retrieval function, but the connection is protected by TLS/SSL so no one can sniff your emails or password in transit.

name: TAILSCALE
title: Tailscale VPN
description: A zero-configuration VPN built on WireGuard. It creates a private network between your devices without complex setup. Popular for securely connecting to home/work computers from anywhere.

name: YANDEX
title: Yandex Services
description: Generic traffic from Yandex, Russia's dominant search engine and internet company. Includes their search engine, maps, and other Yandex services.

name: NTOP
title: ntop Network Probe
description: Traffic from ntop's own network monitoring tools communicating with each other. ntop is the company that created nDPI.

name: COAP
title: Constrained Application Protocol
description: A lightweight web protocol designed for tiny IoT devices with limited memory and power (like sensors). Think of it as HTTP but stripped down to work on a device the size of a coin.

name: VMWARE
title: VMware Virtualization
description: Traffic from VMware's virtualization platform — used to manage virtual machines. VMware lets one physical server run many 'virtual' computers simultaneously.

name: MAIL_SMTPS
title: SMTP Secure (SMTPS)
description: The encrypted version of SMTP for sending email. Your email app uses this to securely transmit your messages so credentials and content can't be intercepted.

name: DTLS
title: Datagram TLS
description: TLS encryption adapted for UDP (datagram-based) traffic. Used to secure real-time communications like VoIP and video calls where speed matters more than guaranteed delivery.

name: UBNTAC2
title: Ubiquiti AirControl 2
description: Network management protocol for Ubiquiti's AirControl 2 software, which manages wireless access points and network equipment.

name: BFCP
title: Binary Floor Control Protocol
description: Manages who has 'the floor' (the right to speak or share screen) in video conferences. When you click 'Request to present' in a video call, BFCP is coordinating that.

name: YANDEX_MAIL
title: Yandex Mail
description: Email traffic for Yandex.Mail, a free email service provided by Russian internet company Yandex.

name: YANDEX_MUSIC
title: Yandex Music
description: Streaming traffic for Yandex Music, a music streaming service similar to Spotify but focused on Russian-language content and popular in Russia/CIS countries.

name: GNUTELLA
title: Gnutella P2P Network
description: A decentralized peer-to-peer file sharing network — no central server. Was hugely popular in the early 2000s (LimeWire used it). Still used for file sharing today.

name: EDONKEY
title: eDonkey P2P Network
description: An older peer-to-peer file sharing network popular in the early 2000s. Known for handling large file transfers. Still has some active users through eMule.

name: BITTORRENT
title: BitTorrent
description: The most popular peer-to-peer file distribution protocol. Instead of downloading from one server, BitTorrent downloads pieces of a file from many users simultaneously, making it extremely efficient for large files.

name: MSTEAMS_CALL
title: Microsoft Teams / Skype Audio-Video Call
description: The real-time audio and video call stream within Microsoft Teams or Skype. This is the media component — the actual voice and video data flowing during a call.

name: SIGNAL
title: Signal Messenger
description: A highly secure, end-to-end encrypted messaging app. Signal is the gold standard for private communications, used by journalists, activists, and privacy-conscious users worldwide.

name: MEMCACHED
title: Memcached Cache Protocol
description: A distributed in-memory cache system. Web applications use Memcached to temporarily store frequently-accessed data in RAM for ultra-fast retrieval, reducing database load.
note: ⚠️ Memcached servers exposed to the internet can be abused for massive DDoS amplification attacks.

name: SMBV23
title: Server Message Block v2/v3
description: Modern Windows file and printer sharing protocol. When you open a shared folder on a Windows network, SMBv2/v3 is what transfers the files. Much more secure than the older SMBv1.

name: MINING
title: Cryptocurrency Mining
description: Traffic from cryptocurrency mining — computers communicating with mining pools to solve cryptographic puzzles and earn coins. If seen on a corporate network unexpectedly, it may indicate unauthorized use or malware.
note: ⚠️ Unexpected mining traffic on a corporate network may indicate unauthorized crypto-jacking malware.

name: NEST_LOG_SINK
title: Nest Log Sink
description: Traffic from Google Nest devices (like Nest Protect smoke detectors) sending log and telemetry data back to Google's cloud servers.

name: MODBUS
title: Modbus Industrial Protocol
description: One of the oldest and most widely used industrial protocols for connecting electronic devices in factories and power plants. Connects PLCs, sensors, and actuators. Originally designed in 1979 with minimal security.
note: ⚠️ Modbus has no authentication. If detected from unexpected sources, investigate immediately.

name: WHATSAPP_CALL
title: WhatsApp Voice/Video Call
description: The audio and video stream during a WhatsApp call. WhatsApp calls are end-to-end encrypted. This specifically identifies the real-time media stream, separate from text messages.

name: DATASAVER
title: Google Chrome Data Saver
description: Traffic routed through Google's servers to compress web pages before delivery, reducing mobile data usage. A feature in older Chrome for Android.

name: XBOX
title: Xbox Gaming Network
description: Traffic from Microsoft Xbox consoles — game downloads, multiplayer matchmaking, Xbox Live services, and the Xbox app on PC.

name: QQ
title: Tencent QQ Messenger
description: China's most popular instant messaging platform by Tencent. QQ offers messaging, video calls, gaming, and social features. Hugely popular in China with hundreds of millions of users.

name: TIKTOK
title: TikTok
description: Traffic from the TikTok short-video app — includes video streaming, uploads, live streams, and API calls. One of the highest-bandwidth social media apps due to continuous video playback.

name: RTSP
title: Real Time Streaming Protocol
description: A control protocol for streaming media servers — think of it as the 'remote control' for a video stream. Used by IP cameras, media servers, and some live streaming systems.

name: MAIL_IMAPS
title: IMAP Secure (IMAPS)
description: Encrypted IMAP — your email client's encrypted connection to fetch and sync mail from the server. The 'S' means TLS encryption protects your login and emails in transit.

name: ICECAST
title: Icecast Streaming Server
description: An open-source audio/video streaming server. Often used by independent internet radio stations and podcasters to broadcast live streams.

name: CPHA
title: Check Point High Availability
description: Protocol used between Check Point firewall devices to synchronize state and provide failover. If one firewall fails, the other takes over seamlessly using CPHA.

name: IQIYI
title: iQIYI Video Streaming
description: China's largest online video platform (owned by Baidu) — comparable to Netflix. Offers movies, TV dramas, anime, and original content. Huge in China and popular across Asia.

name: ZATTOO
title: Zattoo TV Streaming
description: A European live TV streaming service allowing users to watch television channels over the internet.

name: YANDEX_MARKET
title: Yandex Market
description: Russia's largest price comparison and e-commerce platform, similar to Amazon or Google Shopping.

name: YANDEX_DISK
title: Yandex Disk Cloud Storage
description: Cloud file storage service by Yandex, similar to Dropbox or Google Drive. Common in Russia and CIS countries.

name: DISCORD
title: Discord
description: A voice, video, and text communication platform originally popular with gamers, now widely used by communities and teams. Discord uses WebRTC for voice/video and HTTPS for chat.

name: ADOBE_CONNECT
title: Adobe Connect
description: A web conferencing platform for online meetings, webinars, and virtual training. Used in enterprise and education settings.

name: MONGODB
title: MongoDB Database Protocol
description: Traffic to/from a MongoDB database — a popular NoSQL database that stores data in flexible, JSON-like documents rather than rigid tables. Used by many modern web apps.

name: PLURALSIGHT
title: Pluralsight
description: Online technology learning platform offering courses for developers, IT ops, and data professionals.

name: YANDEX_CLOUD
title: Yandex Cloud
description: Yandex's public cloud computing platform offering VMs, storage, databases, and AI services. Russia's main alternative to AWS/Azure/GCP.

name: OCSP
title: Online Certificate Status Protocol
description: Checks whether a website's security certificate is still valid and hasn't been revoked. Your browser uses this in the background every time it connects to an HTTPS site.

name: VXLAN
title: Virtual Extensible LAN
description: A tunneling protocol used in data centers to create virtual networks on top of physical networks. Allows thousands of isolated virtual networks to coexist on the same physical infrastructure.

name: IRC
title: Internet Relay Chat
description: One of the oldest real-time text chat protocols, dating back to 1988. Still used by open-source developers and tech communities. Also historically used by botnets for command and control.
note: ℹ️ IRC is occasionally used by malware botnets for command-and-control communications.

name: MERAKI_CLOUD
title: Cisco Meraki Cloud
description: Traffic from Cisco Meraki network devices (Wi-Fi access points, switches) communicating with Meraki's cloud management platform.

name: JABBER
title: Jabber / XMPP
description: An open, decentralized instant messaging protocol. Unlike proprietary platforms, XMPP lets anyone run their own server. Powers many enterprise chat systems and some consumer apps.

name: NATS
title: NATS Messaging System
description: A high-performance cloud-native messaging system used for building microservices and distributed systems. Devices or services send messages to 'subjects' and subscribers receive them instantly.

name: AMONG_US
title: Among Us
description: Traffic from the multiplayer social deduction game 'Among Us'. Players work together on a spaceship while impostors try to sabotage the mission.

name: YAHOO
title: Yahoo Services
description: Traffic from Yahoo's various internet services including email, news, finance, and search.

name: DISNEYPLUS
title: Disney+
description: Disney's streaming service featuring movies and series from Disney, Marvel, Star Wars, and Pixar. High-bandwidth video streaming traffic.

name: HART_IP
title: HART-IP Industrial Protocol
description: Highway Addressable Remote Transducer — a protocol for communicating with industrial sensors and instruments (pressure sensors, flow meters, etc.) over an IP network.

name: IP_VRRP
title: Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol
description: Allows multiple routers to share a single virtual IP address, providing failover. If the primary router fails, a backup router automatically takes over the shared IP without users noticing.

name: STEAM
title: Steam Gaming Platform
description: Valve's digital game store and gaming network. Steam traffic includes game downloads (can be very large), multiplayer gaming, friends list, and the Steam store.

name: MELSEC
title: Mitsubishi MELSEC Protocol
description: Proprietary communication protocol for Mitsubishi Electric PLCs (Programmable Logic Controllers) used in industrial automation — factory machines, assembly lines, etc.

name: WORLDOFWARCRAFT
title: World of Warcraft
description: Traffic from the iconic massively multiplayer online role-playing game (MMORPG) by Blizzard. WoW has maintained a dedicated player base since 2004.

name: TELNET
title: Telnet Remote Terminal
description: An ancient protocol for remote command-line access to systems. It sends all data including passwords in plain text with no encryption. Replaced by SSH, but still found on legacy systems and IoT devices.
note: ⚠️ Telnet sends passwords in plain text. Use SSH instead. Telnet access from the internet is a serious security risk.

name: STUN
title: Session Traversal Utilities for NAT
description: Helps devices behind a router (NAT) discover their public IP address and establish direct connections for VoIP and video calls. Used by WebRTC, WhatsApp, Zoom, and similar apps.

name: IPSEC
title: IP Security (IPsec)
description: A suite of protocols that encrypt and authenticate IP packets. The foundation of many VPNs. IPsec works at the network layer, meaning it protects all traffic transparently, not just specific apps.

name: IP_GRE
title: Generic Routing Encapsulation
description: A tunneling protocol that wraps (encapsulates) one network packet inside another. Used to create VPN tunnels and route traffic between networks that can't directly communicate.

name: IP_ICMP
title: Internet Control Message Protocol
description: Used for network diagnostics and error reporting. The 'ping' command uses ICMP. When a router can't deliver a packet, it sends an ICMP error back. Essential for troubleshooting.

name: IP_IGMP
title: Internet Group Management Protocol
description: Manages multicast group membership. When you watch a live stream that's sent to multiple viewers simultaneously, IGMP tells your router which multicast streams you want to receive.

name: IP_EGP
title: Exterior Gateway Protocol
description: An obsolete routing protocol replaced by BGP. EGP was used in the early internet to exchange routing information between different networks.

name: IP_SCTP
title: Stream Control Transmission Protocol
description: A transport protocol like TCP, but designed for telecom signaling with features like multi-homing (multiple network paths) and message boundaries. Used in mobile networks.

name: IP_OSPF
title: Open Shortest Path First
description: A link-state routing protocol used within large networks. Routers running OSPF share a complete map of the network and each independently calculates the most efficient path to every destination.

name: IP_IP_IN_IP
title: IP-in-IP Encapsulation
description: Wraps one complete IP packet inside another IP packet's payload. Used for simple tunneling between networks — for example, to connect two separate networks across the internet.

name: RTP
title: Real-time Transport Protocol
description: Carries audio and video data in real time. RTP is the actual media stream in VoIP calls, video conferences, and live streams — it's what carries the actual voice and video content.

name: RDP
title: Remote Desktop Protocol
description: Microsoft's protocol for remotely controlling another Windows computer's graphical desktop. The screen, keyboard, and mouse inputs are all transmitted over the network.
note: ⚠️ RDP exposed to the internet is a prime target for brute-force attacks and ransomware delivery.

name: VNC
title: Virtual Network Computing
description: A platform-independent remote desktop protocol. Lets you see and control another computer's screen over the network. Works across Windows, Mac, and Linux.
note: ⚠️ VNC without strong authentication and encryption is a serious security risk.

name: TUMBLR
title: Tumblr
description: A microblogging and social networking platform known for creative and fandom communities.

name: TLS
title: Transport Layer Security
description: The encryption protocol that powers HTTPS and secures most of the internet. TLS creates an encrypted tunnel between two parties so data can't be read or modified in transit. The padlock in your browser indicates TLS is active.

name: SSH
title: Secure Shell
description: The standard protocol for secure remote command-line access to servers. SSH encrypts everything — your login, commands, and data. It replaced Telnet and is used by every sysadmin and developer worldwide.

name: USENET
title: Usenet Newsgroups
description: A distributed discussion system predating the web. Usenet consists of thousands of 'newsgroups' on various topics. Also used for binary file sharing. Largely superseded by web forums and Reddit.

name: MGCP
title: Media Gateway Control Protocol
description: Controls media gateways that convert voice calls between VoIP and traditional telephone networks. Used in enterprise telephony systems.

name: IAX
title: Inter-Asterisk eXchange
description: A VoIP protocol developed for the open-source Asterisk phone system. IAX2 is efficient for transporting multiple calls and works well through NAT.

name: TFTP
title: Trivial File Transfer Protocol
description: A very simple, lightweight file transfer protocol — no authentication, no directory browsing. Used for booting diskless devices (PXE boot) and loading firmware onto network equipment.
note: ℹ️ TFTP has no authentication — only use on trusted internal networks.

name: AFP
title: Apple Filing Protocol
description: Apple's proprietary network file sharing protocol for macOS. When you connect to a Mac file server, AFP handles the file transfer. Largely replaced by SMB in modern macOS.

name: YANDEX_METRIKA
title: Yandex Metrica
description: Web analytics service by Yandex (similar to Google Analytics) that collects visitor data for websites.

name: YANDEX_DIRECT
title: Yandex Direct Advertising
description: Yandex's online advertising platform — equivalent to Google Ads. Serves contextual ads across Yandex search and partner sites.

name: SIP
title: Session Initiation Protocol
description: The primary protocol for setting up, managing, and ending VoIP phone calls and video sessions. When you make an internet phone call, SIP is the 'dialing' mechanism, while RTP carries the actual voice.

name: TRUPHONE
title: Truphone VoIP
description: A global mobile network operator using VoIP and eSIM technology to provide international calling.

name: IP_ICMPV6
title: ICMPv6
description: The IPv6 version of ICMP — used for diagnostics, error messages, and neighbor discovery (how IPv6 devices find each other on a local network, replacing ARP).

name: DHCPV6
title: DHCPv6
description: Like DHCP but for IPv6 networks — automatically assigns IPv6 addresses and network configuration to devices.

name: ARMAGETRON
title: Armagetron Advanced
description: A free, open-source 3D multiplayer game inspired by the light cycle sequence in the movie Tron.

name: CROSSFIRE
title: Crossfire Online FPS
description: A popular free-to-play online first-person shooter game with a large playerbase in Asia and South America.

name: DOFUS
title: Dofus MMORPG
description: A tactical turn-based MMORPG with a distinctive comic art style, popular in France and globally.

name: BLACKNUT
title: Blacknut Cloud Gaming
description: A cloud gaming subscription service that streams PC games to any device over the internet.

name: BOOSTEROID
title: Boosteroid Cloud Gaming
description: A European cloud gaming service that lets users play high-end PC games on lower-powered devices via streaming.

name: GUILDWARS2
title: Guild Wars 2
description: A popular massively multiplayer online RPG known for its dynamic events, no monthly subscription, and rich PvP content.

name: AMAZON_ALEXA
title: Amazon Alexa Voice Service
description: Traffic from Alexa-enabled smart speakers and devices communicating with Amazon's cloud to process voice commands.

name: KERBEROS
title: Kerberos Authentication
description: A network authentication protocol used in enterprise Windows (Active Directory) environments. When you log into your work computer and instantly access shared drives and email, Kerberos is handling the authentication behind the scenes.

name: LDAP
title: Lightweight Directory Access Protocol
description: A protocol for querying and modifying directory services like Microsoft Active Directory. Used for looking up user accounts, groups, and permissions in corporate environments.

name: NEXON
title: Nexon Games
description: South Korean game publisher and developer with popular titles like MapleStory, Dungeon Fighter Online, and others.

name: MSSQL_TDS
title: Microsoft SQL Server (TDS)
description: The wire protocol used by Microsoft SQL Server — the protocol clients use to send queries and receive results. If you run a .NET app with SQL Server, this is what's flowing.

name: PPTP
title: Point-to-Point Tunneling Protocol
description: An older VPN protocol developed by Microsoft. Creates a secure tunnel for remote access but has known security vulnerabilities and is considered obsolete.
note: ⚠️ PPTP is considered cryptographically broken. Migrate to IKEv2, WireGuard, or OpenVPN.

name: IP_AH
title: IPsec Authentication Header
description: Part of the IPsec framework. AH provides authentication and integrity checking for IP packets — it verifies the packet came from the right sender and wasn't modified, but does NOT encrypt the content.

name: IP_ESP
title: IPsec Encapsulating Security Payload
description: Part of IPsec that provides full encryption plus authentication. ESP is what actually encrypts your VPN traffic. When you use a company VPN, ESP is likely encrypting the data.

name: SLACK
title: Slack
description: A business messaging and collaboration platform. Slack traffic includes real-time messages, file uploads, video calls, and integrations with other business tools.

name: FACEBOOK
title: Facebook / Meta
description: Traffic from Facebook's web and mobile apps — includes newsfeed browsing, photo/video uploads, and various Meta services.

name: TWITTER
title: Twitter / X
description: Traffic from Twitter (now rebranded as X) — tweets, direct messages, media uploads, and API access.

name: DROPBOX
title: Dropbox
description: Cloud storage and file sync service. Dropbox traffic includes file synchronization, sharing, and collaboration — can generate significant bandwidth with large files.

name: GMAIL
title: Gmail
description: Google's email service traffic — web interface, API access, and IMAP/SMTP for email clients. Gmail is one of the most-used email services globally.

name: GOOGLE_MAPS
title: Google Maps
description: Traffic from Google Maps — map tile loading, navigation requests, Street View, and location search.

name: YOUTUBE
title: YouTube
description: The world's largest video platform. YouTube traffic is typically the highest-bandwidth traffic on most networks due to continuous high-definition video streaming.

name: MOZILLA
title: Mozilla / Firefox
description: Traffic related to the Firefox browser — telemetry, add-on updates, Firefox Sync, and Mozilla services.

name: GOOGLE
title: Google Services (Generic)
description: Generic Google traffic not classified under a more specific category (YouTube, Gmail, etc.). Includes Google search, tag manager, analytics, and other Google APIs.

name: MS_RPCH
title: Microsoft RPC over HTTP
description: Tunnels Microsoft Remote Procedure Call traffic over HTTP/HTTPS. Used by Microsoft Exchange and Outlook for email access through firewalls — this is how corporate email worked before Microsoft 365.

name: NETFLOW
title: NetFlow
description: A Cisco protocol for collecting IP network traffic statistics. Routers export flow data (who talked to who, how much data, what protocol) to a NetFlow collector for analysis and monitoring.

name: SFLOW
title: sFlow
description: A packet sampling protocol for real-time network traffic monitoring. Unlike NetFlow which captures all flows, sFlow randomly samples packets — more scalable for high-speed networks.

name: HTTP_CONNECT
title: HTTP CONNECT Tunnel
description: A special HTTP method that tells a proxy server to establish a direct tunnel to a destination. Commonly used to tunnel HTTPS traffic through an HTTP proxy.

name: HTTP_PROXY
title: HTTP Proxy
description: Web traffic passing through an HTTP proxy server — a middleman that receives requests on behalf of clients, used for web filtering, caching, and sometimes anonymization.

name: CITRIX
title: Citrix Virtual Apps
description: Citrix allows users to access applications and desktops hosted on remote servers. Used in enterprises to deliver software to employees without installing it locally.

name: NETFLIX
title: Netflix
description: The world's leading video streaming service. Netflix traffic can be one of the largest bandwidth consumers on a network — streaming 4K video uses ~25 Mbps per stream.

name: LASTFM
title: Last.fm
description: A music discovery and recommendation service that tracks your listening habits and provides personalized recommendations and charts.

name: WAZE
title: Waze Navigation
description: Community-based GPS navigation app with real-time traffic, police, and hazard reports from other drivers.

name: YOUTUBE_UPLOAD
title: YouTube Upload
description: Specifically identifies traffic uploading content to YouTube — distinct from watching videos. Upload traffic is high-bandwidth and outbound.

name: HULU
title: Hulu
description: US streaming service offering live TV, on-demand shows, and original content. Like Netflix but with more current TV episodes.

name: CHECKMK
title: Checkmk Monitoring
description: An IT infrastructure monitoring platform. Checkmk agents installed on servers send health data (CPU, memory, disk, services) to the monitoring server.

name: AJP
title: Apache JServ Protocol
description: Used by web servers (like Apache) to communicate with Java application servers (like Tomcat) behind the scenes. The web server receives requests and forwards them to the app server via AJP.
note: ⚠️ AJP exposed to the internet is dangerous (Apache Ghostcat vulnerability). Block at firewall.

name: APPLE
title: Apple Services
description: Generic Apple ecosystem traffic — updates, iCloud, App Store background traffic, and Apple's various online services.

name: WEBEX
title: Cisco Webex
description: Cisco's video conferencing and collaboration platform. Widely used in enterprises for online meetings, webinars, and team messaging.

name: WHATSAPP
title: WhatsApp
description: Meta's end-to-end encrypted messaging app. WhatsApp text messages, photos, and file transfers. One of the most-used messaging apps globally with over 2 billion users.

name: APPLE_ICLOUD
title: Apple iCloud
description: Apple's cloud storage and sync service. Traffic includes photo library sync, iCloud Drive, device backups, and contacts/calendar sync.

name: VIBER
title: Viber
description: A cross-platform messaging and VoIP application. Viber offers text, voice, and video communication. Very popular in Eastern Europe and the Middle East.

name: APPLE_ITUNES
title: Apple iTunes / Apple Media
description: Traffic from iTunes or Apple's media services — music, podcast, and video content from the Apple ecosystem.

name: RADIUS
title: Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service
description: A networking protocol for centralized authentication, authorization, and accounting (AAA). When you log into a Wi-Fi network with a username/password (not just a Wi-Fi password), RADIUS often handles the authentication.

name: WINDOWS_UPDATE
title: Windows Update
description: Traffic from Windows Update service downloading OS patches and driver updates from Microsoft's servers. Can consume significant bandwidth during large updates.

name: TEAMVIEWER
title: TeamViewer
description: Remote access and control software used for IT support and remote work. An IT technician can see and control your screen using TeamViewer. Traffic is encrypted and relayed through TeamViewer's servers.

name: EGD
title: Ethernet Global Data
description: A protocol for real-time data exchange in industrial automation systems, particularly GE PLC and SCADA systems.

name: HCL_NOTES
title: HCL Notes (Lotus Notes)
description: A collaborative client-server application by HCL (formerly IBM/Lotus). Provides email, calendar, document management, and workflow automation for enterprises.

name: SAP
title: Session Announcement Protocol
description: SAP announces multicast multimedia session information so that potential participants can know about upcoming sessions.

name: GTP
title: GPRS Tunneling Protocol
description: Used in mobile networks (3G/4G/5G) to carry user data and control signaling. When your phone uses mobile data, GTP is what tunnels your IP traffic through the mobile network infrastructure.

name: WSD
title: WS-Discovery
description: A Web Services protocol that allows devices on a local network to find each other automatically — used by Windows to discover printers, scanners, and other devices on your network.

name: LLMNR
title: Link-Local Multicast Name Resolution
description: Allows Windows devices to resolve hostnames on a local network segment without a DNS server. It's a fallback mechanism when DNS fails.
note: ⚠️ LLMNR can be exploited by network attackers for credential theft (LLMNR poisoning). Consider disabling on managed networks.

name: TOCA_BOCA
title: Toca Boca Games
description: Creative and playful mobile games designed for children by Swedish developer Toca Boca.

name: SPOTIFY
title: Spotify
description: The world's most popular music streaming service. Spotify streams audio at up to 320 kbps and also syncs playlists, podcast data, and social features.

name: FACEBOOK_MESSENGER
title: Facebook Messenger
description: Meta's standalone messaging app — text, photos, voice notes, and calls. Separate from Facebook itself, Messenger has its own dedicated traffic patterns.

name: H323
title: H.323 VoIP Standard
description: An older standard for real-time voice, video, and data communications over IP networks. Used in enterprise VoIP systems and video conferencing equipment. Largely replaced by SIP.

name: OPENVPN
title: OpenVPN
description: The most popular open-source VPN protocol. OpenVPN can use either UDP or TCP and typically runs on port 1194. Known for being highly configurable and secure.

name: NOE
title: New Office Environment (VoIP)
description: A proprietary VoIP protocol used in Alcatel-Lucent enterprise telephone systems.

name: CISCOVPN
title: Cisco VPN
description: Cisco's proprietary VPN protocols including Cisco AnyConnect. Widely deployed in enterprises for secure remote access to corporate networks.

name: TEAMSPEAK
title: TeamSpeak
description: A voice-over-IP application designed for gamers. Teams use TeamSpeak for real-time voice communication during gaming sessions — similar to Discord.

name: TOR
title: Tor Anonymity Network
description: The Onion Router — routes traffic through multiple volunteer-operated relays to anonymize internet activity. Each relay only knows the previous and next hop, making tracing very difficult. Used for privacy and to bypass censorship.
note: ℹ️ Tor has legitimate privacy uses but is also used to bypass security controls. Unexpected Tor traffic on corporate networks warrants investigation.

name: SKINNY
title: Skinny Client Control Protocol (SCCP)
description: Cisco's proprietary VoIP signaling protocol for IP phones. Used in Cisco Unified Communications Manager environments — how Cisco IP desk phones register and receive calls.

name: RTCP
title: Real-time Transport Control Protocol
description: Works alongside RTP to provide quality feedback during media streams. RTCP reports packet loss, jitter, and latency so the application can adapt the stream quality.

name: RSYNC
title: Rsync File Synchronization
description: A fast, efficient file transfer and synchronization tool that only transfers the differences between files rather than copying everything. Widely used for backups and deployments.

name: ORACLE
title: Oracle Database
description: Traffic to/from Oracle database servers. Oracle is a leading enterprise database platform used for large-scale transactional and analytical workloads.

name: CORBA
title: CORBA
description: Common Object Request Broker Architecture — an older middleware standard for objects to communicate over a network regardless of programming language or platform.

name: CANONICAL
title: Canonical / Ubuntu
description: Traffic to Canonical's servers — Ubuntu software updates, Snap package downloads, and Canonical cloud services.

name: WHOIS_DAS
title: WHOIS / Domain Assignment Service
description: Protocol for querying domain registration databases — who owns a domain, when it expires, which registrar manages it, etc.

name: SD_RTN
title: Agora SD-RTN
description: Agora's global real-time network (SD-RTN) used for low-latency audio/video streaming in apps built on the Agora SDK — used by many video calling applications.

name: SOCKS
title: SOCKS Proxy
description: A protocol for routing network traffic through a proxy server. SOCKS5 supports authentication and can handle any type of traffic (not just HTTP). Used in privacy tools and sometimes by malware to bypass firewalls.

name: NINTENDO
title: Nintendo Network
description: Traffic from Nintendo gaming consoles (Switch, 3DS) — game downloads, online multiplayer, Nintendo eShop, and friends list.

name: RTMP
title: Real-Time Messaging Protocol
description: Adobe's protocol for streaming audio, video, and data. RTMP was the backbone of Flash video and is still used for live streaming ingest (OBS → Twitch/YouTube uses RTMP).

name: FTP_DATA
title: FTP Data Transfer
description: The data channel of FTP — the actual file bytes being transferred. Separate from FTP_CONTROL which carries commands. You might see both if someone is actively transferring files via FTP.

name: WIKIPEDIA
title: Wikipedia
description: Traffic from accessing Wikipedia, the free online encyclopedia.

name: ZMQ
title: ZeroMQ
description: A high-performance asynchronous messaging library used for building distributed and concurrent applications. ZMQ provides messaging patterns (push/pull, pub/sub, request/reply) without a central message broker.

name: AMAZON
title: Amazon (Generic)
description: Generic Amazon traffic — retail website, Amazon Prime, and Amazon's various services not classified under a specific AWS service.

name: EBAY
title: eBay
description: Traffic from the eBay online marketplace — browsing listings, auctions, and purchases.

name: CNN
title: CNN News
description: Traffic from CNN's website and apps — news articles and video streaming.

name: MEGACO
title: Megaco / H.248
description: A protocol for controlling media gateways in VoIP infrastructure — the signaling between a call agent and a gateway that converts VoIP to traditional telephone networks.

name: RESP
title: Redis Serialization Protocol
description: The protocol used to communicate with Redis — an ultra-fast in-memory data store. Redis is used as a cache, message broker, and session store by high-performance web applications.

name: PINTEREST
title: Pinterest
description: A visual discovery and bookmarking platform where users save and share images and ideas organized into 'boards'.

name: OSPF
title: OSPF (Application-level)
description: Open Shortest Path First routing protocol traffic. Same as IP_OSPF (#85) but detected at the application layer. Routers exchange link state information to build network topology maps.

name: TELEGRAM
title: Telegram
description: A cloud-based instant messaging app with a focus on speed and security. Known for large group chats, channels, and bots. Telegram's MTProto protocol provides end-to-end encryption for secret chats.

name: COD_MOBILE
title: Call of Duty: Mobile
description: The mobile version of the popular Call of Duty franchise — a first-person shooter with battle royale and multiplayer modes.

name: PANDORA
title: Pandora
description: An internet radio and music streaming service (US-focused). Pandora pioneered personalized internet radio by learning your music tastes.

name: QUIC
title: QUIC Transport Protocol
description: A modern transport protocol developed by Google, now standardized as HTTP/3. QUIC runs over UDP and dramatically speeds up web connections by eliminating TCP's connection setup delays. Most modern browsers and Google services use QUIC.

name: ZOOM
title: Zoom
description: Video conferencing platform that became ubiquitous for remote work. Zoom uses a mix of TCP and UDP for signaling and media, and is optimized for reliability even on poor connections.

name: EAQ
title: EAQ Broadband Quality
description: Traffic from Brazil's national broadband quality measurement initiative.

name: OOKLA
title: Ookla Speedtest
description: Traffic from Speedtest.net speed tests. Ookla measures your internet connection speed by downloading and uploading test data to nearby servers.

name: AMQP
title: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol
description: An open-source messaging protocol used for sending messages between applications. AMQP powers RabbitMQ and is used for decoupling microservices, task queues, and event streaming.

name: KAKAOTALK
title: KakaoTalk
description: South Korea's dominant messaging app with over 90% market penetration. KakaoTalk offers text messaging, voice/video calls, and payment services.

name: KAKAOTALK_VOICE
title: KakaoTalk Voice/Video Call
description: The voice and video call stream within KakaoTalk — distinguished from text message traffic.

name: TWITCH
title: Twitch
description: The leading live streaming platform for gaming, esports, and creative content. Twitch streams are high-bandwidth — live streams and VODs consume significant bandwidth.

name: DOH_DOT
title: DNS over HTTPS / TLS / QUIC
description: Encrypted DNS — your DNS queries are wrapped in HTTPS, TLS, or QUIC so your ISP and network operators can't see which websites you're looking up. Used by Firefox, Chrome, and various privacy tools.

name: WECHAT
title: WeChat
description: China's 'super-app' — messaging, social media, mobile payments, and mini-apps all in one. WeChat is essential for daily life in China with over 1 billion monthly active users.

name: MPEGTS
title: MPEG Transport Stream
description: A container format for transmitting audio, video, and data. Used for digital TV broadcasting, IPTV, and sometimes live streaming. The format that carries HD digital TV signals.

name: SNAPCHAT
title: Snapchat
description: A multimedia messaging app known for disappearing messages and Stories. Snapchat's AR filters and Spotlight video feed generate significant traffic.

name: SINA
title: Sina
description: Chinese internet company operating Sina Weibo (China's Twitter equivalent) and other web portals.

name: GOOGLE_MEET
title: Google Meet
description: Google's video conferencing service integrated with Gmail and Google Calendar. Used widely in education and business.

name: IFLIX
title: iflix
description: A video-on-demand service for Southeast Asia, offering local and international content.

name: GITHUB
title: GitHub
description: The world's largest code hosting and collaboration platform. GitHub traffic includes repository browsing, git operations, CI/CD pipelines, and GitHub Copilot.

name: BJNP
title: Canon BJNP Printer Protocol
description: Canon's proprietary printer discovery and communication protocol used by inkjet printers on IP networks.

name: REDDIT
title: Reddit
description: A social news aggregation and discussion website. Reddit traffic includes browsing posts, viewing media, and API access by third-party apps.

name: WIREGUARD
title: WireGuard VPN
description: A modern, extremely fast VPN protocol. WireGuard's codebase is tiny (compared to OpenVPN), making it easier to audit and faster in practice. The basis of Tailscale and many commercial VPNs.

name: SMPP
title: Short Message Peer-to-Peer
description: The protocol used between SMS gateways and mobile carriers to exchange SMS messages at high volume. When you send an SMS from an app, SMPP is often used behind the scenes.

name: DNSCRYPT
title: DNSCrypt
description: A protocol that authenticates and encrypts DNS traffic between your device and the DNS resolver, preventing tampering and eavesdropping on DNS queries.

name: TINC
title: Tinc VPN
description: An open-source VPN daemon that creates a secure private network. Tinc supports mesh networking — each node can communicate directly with any other, not just through a central server.

name: DEEZER
title: Deezer
description: A music streaming service offering 90 million tracks. Popular in France and Europe.

name: INSTAGRAM
title: Instagram
description: Meta's photo and video sharing platform. Instagram traffic includes feed scrolling, Stories, Reels, and DMs — Reels generate particularly high video bandwidth.

name: MICROSOFT
title: Microsoft (Generic)
description: Generic Microsoft traffic not classified under a more specific category like Teams, Office 365, or OneDrive.

name: BLIZZARD
title: Blizzard Entertainment
description: Game traffic from Blizzard's games and Battle.net platform — World of Warcraft, Diablo, Overwatch, StarCraft, and Hearthstone.

name: TEREDO
title: Teredo IPv6 Tunneling
description: Microsoft's IPv6 transition technology. Teredo tunnels IPv6 packets inside IPv4 UDP packets, allowing IPv6 connectivity even through NAT devices. Used when native IPv6 isn't available.

name: HOTSPOT_SHIELD
title: Hotspot Shield VPN
description: A consumer VPN service providing encrypted internet connections and IP masking.

name: IMO
title: imo
description: A free video calling and messaging app popular in countries with limited bandwidth and expensive data — optimized for low-quality connections.

name: GOOGLE_DRIVE
title: Google Drive
description: Google's cloud storage and file sync service. Traffic includes file uploads, downloads, and collaborative editing of Google Docs/Sheets/Slides.

name: OCS
title: Office Communications Server
description: Microsoft's predecessor to Lync/Skype for Business. Enterprise instant messaging and presence platform.

name: MICROSOFT_365
title: Microsoft 365
description: Traffic from Microsoft's cloud productivity suite — Word, Excel, PowerPoint Online, SharePoint, Teams, and Exchange Online all generate M365 traffic.

name: CLOUDFLARE
title: Cloudflare
description: Web infrastructure and security company providing CDN, DDoS protection, and DNS services. Traffic from websites using Cloudflare's network will appear as Cloudflare traffic.

name: MS_ONE_DRIVE
title: Microsoft OneDrive
description: Microsoft's cloud storage service integrated with Windows and Microsoft 365. Traffic includes file syncing, sharing, and the OneDrive app on all platforms.

name: MQTT
title: MQTT (IoT Messaging)
description: A lightweight publish-subscribe messaging protocol designed for constrained IoT devices on unreliable networks. Used by smart home devices, industrial sensors, and mobile apps to send small messages efficiently.

name: RX
title: AFS RX Protocol
description: Remote Execution protocol from Carnegie Mellon's Andrew File System. An RPC mechanism used by AFS for remote file access in academic computing environments.

name: APPLESTORE
title: Apple App Store
description: Traffic from the Apple App Store — app downloads, updates, in-app purchases, and App Store browsing on iOS/macOS devices.

name: OPENDNS
title: OpenDNS / Cisco Umbrella
description: Cisco's cloud-delivered DNS security service that filters malicious domains and provides web content filtering.

name: GIT
title: Git Protocol
description: The native Git protocol for cloning, fetching, and pushing code repositories. Used with git:// URLs (port 9418). HTTPS Git traffic is classified as HTTP/TLS instead.

name: DRDA
title: IBM DRDA Database Protocol
description: Distributed Relational Database Architecture — IBM's protocol for distributed database communication. Used by IBM DB2 and other IBM database systems.

name: PLAYSTORE
title: Google Play Store
description: Traffic from the Google Play Store on Android devices — app downloads, updates, in-app purchases, and Play Services communication.

name: SOMEIP
title: SOME/IP Automotive Protocol
description: Scalable service-Oriented MiddlewarE over IP — an automotive protocol for communication between electronic control units (ECUs) in vehicles. When your car's different computers talk to each other over IP, this is often the protocol.

name: FIX
title: Financial Information eXchange
description: The industry-standard messaging protocol for electronic securities trading. When stocks are bought and sold electronically on financial markets, FIX protocol is often what carries the order messages.

name: PLAYSTATION
title: PlayStation Network
description: Sony's gaming network for PS4/PS5 — game downloads, multiplayer gaming, PlayStation Store, and PlayStation Now streaming.

name: PASTEBIN
title: Pastebin
description: A website for storing and sharing text snippets. Used by developers for sharing code, by security researchers for analysis, and sometimes by malware for hosting payloads.
note: ℹ️ Pastebin is occasionally used by malware to host payloads or exfiltrate data.

name: LINKEDIN
title: LinkedIn
description: Microsoft-owned professional networking platform for careers, business connections, and professional content.

name: SOUNDCLOUD
title: SoundCloud
description: An audio streaming platform popular with independent artists for sharing and distributing music, podcasts, and audio content.

name: VALVE_SDR
title: Steam Datagram Relay
description: Valve's private gaming network for Steam games. SDR routes game traffic through Valve's global server network for better performance and DDoS protection. Used by games like Dota 2 and CS:GO.

name: LISP
title: LISP (Locator/ID Separation)
description: A network architecture protocol that separates IP addresses into two roles: where you are (locator) and who you are (identifier). Improves routing scalability for large networks.

name: DIAMETER
title: Diameter AAA Protocol
description: The successor to RADIUS for network authentication, authorization, and accounting. Widely used in mobile networks (LTE/4G/5G) for authenticating subscribers.

name: APPLE_PUSH
title: Apple Push Notification Service
description: Apple's system for delivering push notifications to iPhones, iPads, and Macs. Every app notification on your Apple device travels through APNs.

name: GOOGLE_SERVICES
title: Google Services (APIs)
description: Various Google API endpoints and services including Google Analytics, Tag Manager, Fonts, reCAPTCHA, and other Google platform services.

name: AMAZON_VIDEO
title: Amazon Prime Video
description: Amazon's video streaming service offering movies, TV shows, and Amazon Originals. One of the major competing streaming platforms to Netflix.

name: GOOGLE_DOCS
title: Google Docs
description: Google's online document editing suite (Docs, Sheets, Slides). Supports real-time collaborative editing. Traffic includes document sync, collaboration messages, and media.

name: WHATSAPP_FILES
title: WhatsApp Media Files
description: Media files (photos, videos, voice messages, documents) sent via WhatsApp. This is distinct from WhatsApp text messages and uses different servers optimized for media delivery.

name: TARGUS_GETDATA
title: Targus GetData
description: Proprietary protocol used by Targus devices for data transfer.

name: DNP3
title: DNP3 (Distributed Network Protocol)
description: A communication protocol used in SCADA and process automation — primarily for electric utilities and water treatment plants. DNP3 connects master controllers with remote terminal units (RTUs) at substations.
note: ⚠️ DNP3 has limited built-in security. Critical infrastructure systems using DNP3 must be network-isolated.

name: IEC60870
title: IEC 60870-5-104
description: International standard protocol for telecontrol and supervision in power systems. Used by electricity grid operators to control substations and monitor power equipment remotely.

name: BLOOMBERG
title: Bloomberg Terminal
description: Traffic from Bloomberg's financial data and analytics platform — real-time market data, news, and messaging used by financial professionals.

name: CAPWAP
title: CAPWAP (Wi-Fi AP Management)
description: Control and Provisioning of Wireless Access Points — allows a central wireless LAN controller (WLC) to manage many Wi-Fi access points. Used in enterprise Wi-Fi deployments.

name: ZABBIX
title: Zabbix Monitoring
description: Monitoring platform for networks, servers, and cloud infrastructure. Zabbix agents on monitored hosts send metrics (CPU, memory, network stats) to the Zabbix server.

name: S7COMM
title: Siemens S7 Communication
description: Siemens' proprietary protocol for communicating with SIMATIC S7 PLCs (Programmable Logic Controllers) used in industrial automation. Very common in manufacturing and critical infrastructure.
note: ⚠️ S7comm was targeted by the Stuxnet worm. Industrial networks using S7 should be strictly segmented.

name: MSTEAMS
title: Microsoft Teams
description: Microsoft's collaboration hub combining chat, video meetings, calling, and file collaboration. The primary successor to Skype for Business in enterprises.

name: WEBSOCKET
title: WebSocket
description: A protocol providing full-duplex, bi-directional communication over a single TCP connection. Unlike HTTP where you request-then-respond, WebSocket lets the server push data to the client at any time. Used for live chat, gaming, and real-time apps.

name: ANYDESK
title: AnyDesk
description: A remote desktop application with very low latency even over slow connections. Provides screen sharing and remote control for IT support.

name: SOAP
title: SOAP Web Services
description: Simple Object Access Protocol — an XML-based protocol for exchanging structured data between services. Used in enterprise web services and older API integrations.

name: APPLE_SIRI
title: Apple Siri
description: Traffic from Apple's voice assistant. When you ask Siri a question, audio is sent to Apple's servers for processing and the response comes back.

name: SNAPCHAT_CALL
title: Snapchat Voice/Video Call
description: The real-time audio and video call stream within Snapchat — distinct from Snapchat's photo/message traffic.

name: HPVIRTGRP
title: HP Virtual Group
description: HP's proprietary virtualization communication protocol used in HP server and storage management systems.

name: GENSHIN_IMPACT
title: Genshin Impact
description: A popular open-world action RPG with live-service content. Genshin Impact generates substantial network traffic due to its real-time multiplayer and frequent content updates.

name: ACTIVISION
title: Activision Games
description: Traffic from Activision game titles and the Battlenet platform — Call of Duty (console/PC), Warzone, and other Activision titles.

name: FORTICLIENT
title: Fortinet FortiClient
description: Fortinet's endpoint security and VPN client. Provides secure remote access to corporate networks using SSL-VPN and IPsec.

name: Z3950
title: Z39.50 Library Protocol
description: A client-server protocol for searching and retrieving information from databases — primarily used by libraries for catalog searches.

name: LIKEE
title: Likee
description: A short-video creation and sharing platform popular in Southeast Asia and the Middle East.

name: GITLAB
title: GitLab
description: A DevOps platform providing Git repository management, CI/CD pipelines, and project management — can be self-hosted or cloud-based.

name: AVAST_SECUREDNS
title: Avast Secure DNS
description: Avast's encrypted DNS service that blocks malicious domains as part of their security suite.

name: CASSANDRA
title: Apache Cassandra
description: A distributed NoSQL database system designed for handling huge amounts of data across many servers. Used by companies like Netflix, Instagram, and Uber.

name: AMAZON_AWS
title: Amazon Web Services
description: Generic traffic to/from Amazon Web Services cloud infrastructure. AWS hosts a significant portion of the internet.

name: SALESFORCE
title: Salesforce
description: The leading cloud-based CRM (Customer Relationship Management) platform. Salesforce traffic includes user interaction, API calls, and data sync.

name: VIMEO
title: Vimeo
description: A video hosting platform focused on high-quality, creator-focused video. Popular with filmmakers, agencies, and professionals.

name: FACEBOOK_VOIP
title: Facebook Messenger Voice/Video
description: Voice and video calls made through Facebook Messenger. Distinct from text messaging — this is the real-time media stream.

name: SIGNAL_VOIP
title: Signal Voice/Video Call
description: Encrypted voice and video calls within the Signal messaging app. Signal calls are end-to-end encrypted using the same Signal Protocol as messages.

name: FUZE
title: Fuze
description: A unified communications platform for enterprise video conferencing and collaboration.

name: GTP_U
title: GTP-U (User Plane)
description: GTP User Plane — carries the actual user data (your internet traffic) through the mobile network. Separate from GTP-C which handles control signaling.

name: GTP_C
title: GTP-C (Control Plane)
description: GTP Control Plane — manages tunnel establishment, modification, and deletion in mobile networks. This is the signaling layer, not the actual data.

name: GTP_PRIME
title: GTP Prime (Charging)
description: GTP Prime is used for billing and charging in LTE networks — tracks what data you use for billing purposes.

name: ALIBABA
title: Alibaba
description: Traffic from Alibaba's e-commerce and cloud platforms — Alibaba.com, Taobao parent traffic, and Alibaba Cloud services.

name: CRASHLYSTICS
title: Google Crashlytics
description: Google Firebase's crash reporting tool. When an app crashes, Crashlytics captures and uploads the crash details to help developers fix bugs.

name: MICROSOFT_AZURE
title: Microsoft Azure
description: Microsoft's cloud computing platform. Azure hosts applications, databases, virtual machines, and services. A huge portion of enterprise traffic goes through Azure.

name: ICLOUD_PRIVATE_RELAY
title: iCloud Private Relay
description: Apple's privacy feature that routes your internet traffic through two separate relays — Apple knows where you are but not what you're accessing, and Apple's partner knows what you're accessing but not who you are.

name: ETHERNET_IP
title: Ethernet/IP Industrial Protocol
description: Adapts the Common Industrial Protocol (CIP) to run over standard Ethernet. Used in industrial automation for connecting PLCs, sensors, drives, and HMIs.

name: BADOO
title: Badoo
description: A social networking and dating service with a large user base in Europe and Latin America.

name: ACCUWEATHER
title: AccuWeather
description: Weather forecast service traffic from AccuWeather apps and widgets fetching current conditions and forecasts.

name: GOOGLE_CLASSROOM
title: Google Classroom
description: Google's educational platform for managing assignments, communication between teachers and students, and learning resources.

name: HSRP
title: Hot Standby Router Protocol
description: Cisco's redundancy protocol that groups routers together under a single virtual IP. If the active router fails, a standby router takes over automatically. Provides seamless failover.

name: CYBERSECURITY
title: Cybersecurity Services
description: Traffic to/from cybersecurity vendors — threat intelligence feeds, antivirus updates, security software telemetry, and malware analysis services.

name: GOOGLE_CLOUD
title: Google Cloud Platform
description: Google's cloud computing infrastructure. GCP hosts applications, databases, and services. Traffic classified as Google Cloud (not under a more specific Google service).

name: TENCENT
title: Tencent (Generic)
description: Generic traffic from Tencent's various services — the Chinese conglomerate behind WeChat, QQ, and many games.

name: RAKNET
title: RakNet Game Networking
description: A C++ networking library used by many games for multiplayer networking. Roblox uses a customized version of RakNet. Provides features like reliable UDP, NAT traversal, and encryption.

name: XIAOMI
title: Xiaomi Devices
description: Traffic from Xiaomi smart home devices, phones, and IoT products communicating with Xiaomi's cloud services.

name: EDGECAST
title: Edgio (EdgeCast) CDN
description: A content delivery network providing global content acceleration. Websites serving their content via EdgeCast/Edgio will appear as this protocol.

name: CACHEFLY
title: CacheFly CDN
description: A content delivery network specializing in video streaming delivery.

name: SOFTETHER
title: SoftEther VPN
description: A powerful open-source VPN software supporting multiple protocols: SSL-VPN, L2TP/IPsec, OpenVPN, and more. Often used to bypass VPN restrictions because it disguises traffic as HTTPS.

name: MPEGDASH
title: MPEG-DASH Adaptive Streaming
description: Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP — the standard for adaptive bitrate video streaming. YouTube, Netflix, and Amazon Prime use DASH to automatically adjust video quality based on your connection speed.

name: DAZN
title: DAZN Sports Streaming
description: A subscription sports streaming service broadcasting live and on-demand sports content including boxing, football, motorsports, and more.

name: GOTO
title: GoTo (GoToMeeting/LogMeIn)
description: GoTo's suite of collaboration tools including GoToMeeting, GoToWebinar, and GoToConnect for online meetings and remote access.

name: RSH
title: Remote Shell (rsh)
description: An older protocol for executing shell commands on remote systems. Like Telnet, rsh sends data unencrypted. Completely replaced by SSH in modern systems.
note: ⚠️ rsh has no encryption. Use SSH instead.

name: 1KXUN
title: 1Kxun Streaming
description: A Chinese internet streaming service.

name: IP_PGM
title: Pragmatic General Multicast
description: A reliable multicast transport protocol for one-to-many data distribution with error recovery.

name: IP_PIM
title: Protocol Independent Multicast
description: A family of multicast routing protocols. PIM determines how multicast traffic is routed through a network — used for IPTV distribution, videoconferencing infrastructure, and stock tickers.

name: COLLECTD
title: Collectd Metrics
description: A daemon that periodically collects system and application performance metrics and sends them to a central monitoring system.

name: TUNNELBEAR
title: TunnelBear VPN
description: A consumer-friendly VPN service with a simple bear-themed interface. Provides encrypted tunneling for privacy.

name: CLOUDFLARE_WARP
title: Cloudflare WARP
description: Cloudflare's VPN/secure DNS service using the WireGuard protocol. Routes traffic through Cloudflare's network for privacy and performance.

name: I3D
title: i3D Game Servers
description: i3D.net provides dedicated and cloud game servers optimized for low-latency multiplayer gaming.

name: RIOTGAMES
title: Riot Games
description: Traffic from Riot Games' titles — League of Legends, Valorant, Teamfight Tactics, and others. Uses custom UDP protocols optimized for competitive gaming.

name: PSIPHON
title: Psiphon
description: A free censorship-circumvention tool using a combination of VPN, SSH, and HTTP proxy technologies. Designed for users in countries with heavy internet censorship.

name: ULTRASURF
title: UltraSurf
description: A censorship circumvention tool that uses proxy servers to bypass internet restrictions and firewalls.

name: THREEMA
title: Threema
description: A privacy-focused encrypted messaging app that doesn't require a phone number. Threema stores minimal data and uses end-to-end encryption for all communications.

name: ALICLOUD
title: Alibaba Cloud
description: Alibaba's cloud computing platform — China's largest cloud provider, also with global presence.

name: AVAST
title: Avast Security
description: Traffic from Avast antivirus and security software — signature updates, cloud scanning, and telemetry.

name: TIVOCONNECT
title: TiVo Connect
description: TiVo's proprietary protocol for streaming and device management between TiVo DVRs and connected devices.

name: KISMET
title: Kismet Wireless Monitor
description: Kismet is a wireless network detector and packet sniffer. Traffic from Kismet sensors reporting wireless network data to a Kismet server.

name: FASTCGI
title: FastCGI
description: A protocol that allows web servers to communicate with backend application processes efficiently. PHP-FPM (the standard way to run PHP with Nginx) uses FastCGI.

name: FTPS
title: FTP Secure (FTPS)
description: FTP extended with TLS/SSL encryption. Provides the file transfer capability of FTP with encryption protecting credentials and data in transit.

name: NATPMP
title: NAT Port Mapping Protocol
description: Automatically configures port forwarding on NAT gateways. Similar to UPnP but simpler. Used by apps that need inbound connections to work through a router.

name: SYNCTHING
title: Syncthing
description: An open-source, decentralized file synchronization tool. Syncs files directly between your devices without going through a central server.

name: CRYNET
title: CryEngine Network
description: CryNetwork is the proprietary multiplayer networking protocol used in games built with CryEngine (like the early Crysis games).

name: LINE
title: LINE
description: A messaging app dominant in Japan, Taiwan, and Thailand. LINE offers messaging, voice/video calls, a news feed, payment services, and mini-games.

name: LINE_CALL
title: LINE Voice/Video Call
description: Real-time voice and video call streams within the LINE app, distinct from LINE's text messaging traffic.

name: APPLETVPLUS
title: Apple TV+
description: Apple's streaming service for original movies and TV shows. All content is Apple Originals.

name: DIRECTV
title: DirecTV
description: DirecTV's satellite TV and streaming service traffic.

name: HBO
title: HBO / Max

name: LIVESTREAM

description: A platform for broadcasting live video events online.

name: TENCENTVIDEO
title: Tencent Video

name: IHEARTRADIO
title: iHeartRadio

name: TIDAL
title: Tidal

name: TUNEIN
title: TuneIn Radio
description: A streaming service for live radio stations, sports play-by-play, news, and podcasts from around the world.

name: SIRIUSXMRADIO
title: SiriusXM

name: MUNIN

name: ELASTICSEARCH
