name: TUYA_LP
title: Tuya LAN Protocol
description: Tuya's local area network protocol for controlling Tuya-based smart home devices (many budget smart home brands use the Tuya platform) directly without going through the cloud.

name: TPLINK_SHP
title: TP-Link Smart Home Protocol
description: TP-Link's protocol for local control of Kasa smart home devices (smart plugs, bulbs, switches) on your home network.

name: SOURCE_ENGINE
title: Valve Source Engine (A2S)
description: Valve's UDP-based game server query protocol for Source Engine games (CS:GO, Team Fortress 2, Left 4 Dead). Used to query server info like player count and map name.

name: BACNET
title: BACnet Building Automation
description: Building Automation and Control Networks protocol — used to connect and control HVAC, lighting, fire, and security systems in commercial buildings.

name: OICQ
title: OICQ (QQ Legacy)
description: The original name for Tencent's QQ instant messaging protocol — now synonymous with QQ itself.

name: HOTS
title: Heroes of the Storm
description: Blizzard's free-to-play MOBA (Multiplayer Online Battle Arena) game.

name: FACEBOOK_REEL_STORY
title: Facebook Reels/Stories
description: Short video content (Reels) and Stories on Facebook — video segments streamed for this specific content type.

name: SRTP
title: Secure RTP
description: Encrypted version of RTP — adds encryption and authentication to real-time audio/video streams. Used in secure VoIP calls and encrypted video conferencing.

name: OPERA_VPN
title: Opera Browser VPN
description: The free VPN feature built into Opera's browser. Routes traffic through Opera's proxy servers.

name: EPICGAMES
title: Epic Games
description: Traffic from Epic Games' launcher and games — Fortnite, Rocket League, and other Epic titles, plus the Epic Games Store.

name: GEFORCENOW
title: GeForce Now
description: Nvidia's cloud gaming service that streams PC games to any device over the internet. High-bandwidth real-time gaming video streams.

name: NVIDIA
title: Nvidia Services
description: Generic Nvidia traffic — driver updates, GeForce Experience telemetry, and Nvidia cloud service communications.

name: BITCOIN
title: Bitcoin Network
description: Traffic from Bitcoin node-to-node communication — block propagation, transaction broadcasting, and peer discovery on the Bitcoin network.

name: PROTONVPN
title: ProtonVPN
description: VPN service by Proton AG (the company behind ProtonMail). ProtonVPN is based in Switzerland and uses WireGuard, OpenVPN, and IKEv2.

name: APACHE_THRIFT
title: Apache Thrift
description: A cross-language serialization and RPC framework. Services built with Thrift can communicate across different programming languages using an IDL-defined interface.

name: ROBLOX
title: Roblox
description: A massive online game platform and game creation system, extremely popular with children and teenagers. Roblox uses a modified version of RakNet for networking.

name: SERVICE_LOCATION
title: Service Location Protocol
description: Enables devices to find network services automatically without knowing their addresses in advance — like a yellow pages for network services.

name: MULLVAD
title: Mullvad VPN
description: A highly privacy-focused VPN from Sweden that accepts cash and cryptocurrency. Mullvad doesn't require an email address — you get an account number.

name: HTTP2
title: HTTP/2
description: A major revision of HTTP that allows multiple requests to be sent simultaneously over a single connection (multiplexing). Dramatically speeds up loading of complex webpages. Nearly always runs over TLS.

name: HAPROXY
title: HAProxy
description: A high-performance load balancer and TCP/HTTP proxy. HAProxy is the industry standard for distributing traffic across multiple servers. Detected via its protocol health check format.

name: RMCP
title: IPMI RMCP
description: Remote Management Control Protocol used by IPMI (Intelligent Platform Management Interface) for out-of-band server management — controlling servers when the OS isn't running.

name: CAN
title: Controller Area Network
description: A bus protocol developed for automotive applications. CAN allows microcontrollers in a vehicle to communicate without a host computer — your car's engine, brakes, and other systems talk to each other over CAN.

name: PROTOBUF
title: Protocol Buffers
description: Google's efficient, binary data serialization format. Many Google services and gRPC APIs use Protobuf to encode data compactly for transmission.

name: ETHEREUM
title: Ethereum Network
description: Traffic from the Ethereum blockchain network — node communication, transaction broadcasting, and block propagation. Ethereum also supports smart contracts.

name: TELEGRAM_VOIP
title: Telegram Voice/Video Call
description: Encrypted audio and video calls within Telegram — separate from Telegram's text messaging traffic. Calls are end-to-end encrypted.

name: SINA_WEIBO
title: Sina Weibo
description: China's leading microblogging platform — often called 'China's Twitter'. Weibo has hundreds of millions of active users.

name: TESLA_SERVICES
title: Tesla Services
description: Traffic from Tesla vehicles and apps — vehicle telemetry, over-the-air software updates, navigation data, Sentry Mode uploads, and mobile app communication.

name: PTPV2
title: Precision Time Protocol v2
description: IEEE 1588 PTP provides sub-microsecond clock synchronization between networked devices. Used in telecoms, finance, industrial automation, and anywhere nanosecond timing matters.

name: RTPS
title: Real-Time Publish Subscribe Protocol
description: The wire protocol underlying the Data Distribution Service (DDS) middleware, used in robotics (ROS2), defense systems, and industrial automation for real-time data sharing.

name: OPC_UA
title: OPC Unified Architecture
description: The modern standard for industrial device interoperability. OPC UA allows SCADA systems, PLCs, historians, and MES systems to communicate securely regardless of manufacturer.

name: S7COMM_PLUS
title: Siemens S7comm Plus
description: Siemens' updated S7 protocol for newer PLCs (S7-1200/1500). More secure than classic S7comm with challenge-response authentication.

name: FINS
title: FINS (Omron PLC Protocol)
description: Factory Interface Network Service — Omron's protocol for communicating with their PLCs and industrial devices.

name: ETHERSIO
title: Ether-S-I/O
description: A protocol used by Saia-Burgess PLC products for I/O data exchange.

name: UMAS
title: UMAS (Schneider Electric)
description: Schneider Electric's proprietary protocol based on Modbus. Used in their Modicon PLCs for advanced operations.

name: BECKHOFF_ADS
title: Beckhoff ADS Protocol
description: Automation Device Specification — Beckhoff's protocol for communicating with their TwinCAT PLC systems. Used to read/write PLC variables from applications.

name: ISO9506_1_MMS
title: Manufacturing Message Specification
description: ISO/IEC 9506 MMS enables remote control of industrial devices. Used in electrical power systems for IEC 61850 communication.

name: IEEE_C37118
title: IEEE C37.118 Synchrophasor
description: Standard for transmitting synchrophasor data from PMUs (Phasor Measurement Units) in electrical grids. Used for real-time wide-area monitoring of power system stability.

name: ETHERSBUS
title: Ether-S-Bus
description: Saia-Burgess Ether S-Bus protocol for PLC communication.

name: MONERO
title: Monero Network
description: Traffic from the Monero (XMR) cryptocurrency network — a privacy-focused cryptocurrency where transactions are untraceable by design.

name: DCERPC
title: DCE/RPC
description: Distributed Computing Environment Remote Procedure Call — the mechanism underlying many Windows network services. Active Directory and file sharing rely heavily on DCE/RPC.

name: PROFINET_IO
title: PROFINET Industrial Ethernet
description: A standard for industrial Ethernet used extensively in factory automation. PROFINET connects PLCs to field devices like drives, I/O modules, and sensors in real time.

detection.label: DCE/RPC over UDP with PROFINET UUID

name: HISLIP
title: HiSLIP
description: High-Speed LAN Instrument Protocol for remote control of test and measurement equipment (oscilloscopes, signal generators, etc.) over a local network.

name: UFTP
title: UFTP (Multicast FTP)
description: Encrypted UDP-based FTP with multicast support. Designed for efficient simultaneous file distribution to many recipients.

name: OPENFLOW
title: OpenFlow (SDN)
description: A protocol for Software-Defined Networking (SDN). OpenFlow allows a central controller to manage the forwarding rules on network switches, separating the control plane from the data plane.

name: JSON_RPC
title: JSON-RPC
description: A remote procedure call protocol using JSON encoding. Commonly used by cryptocurrency nodes (Bitcoin, Ethereum local APIs), IoT devices, and simple microservices.

name: WEBDAV
title: WebDAV
description: Web Distributed Authoring and Versioning — extends HTTP to allow creating, editing, and managing files on web servers. Used by some cloud storage services and Windows network drive mapping.

name: APACHE_KAFKA
title: Apache Kafka
description: A distributed event streaming platform. Kafka acts as a high-throughput message bus — producers write events, consumers read them. Used by LinkedIn, Uber, and Netflix for real-time data pipelines.

name: NOMACHINE
title: NoMachine
description: A proprietary remote desktop software known for extremely low latency, making it feel like you're sitting at the remote machine.

name: IEC62056
title: IEC 62056 Smart Metering
description: Standard for smart electricity meter data exchange using DLMS/COSEM. Used by energy utilities to read smart meters remotely.

name: HL7
title: HL7 Healthcare Messaging
description: A set of standards for exchanging clinical and administrative health data between hospital systems — patient records, lab results, and medication orders.

name: CEPH
title: Ceph Distributed Storage
description: A scalable distributed storage system providing object, block, and file storage. Used in enterprise and cloud environments for large-scale storage clusters.

name: GOOGLE_CHAT
title: Google Chat
description: Google's business messaging platform, integrated with Gmail and Google Workspace. Successor to Google Hangouts for team communication.

name: ROUGHTIME
title: Roughtime
description: A protocol for coarse time synchronization with cryptographic proof that the server actually provided the time — prevents time-based attacks.

name: PIA
title: Private Internet Access VPN
description: A popular VPN service known for its large server network and no-logs policy.

name: KCP
title: KCP Protocol
description: A fast, reliable protocol that provides TCP-like reliability with lower latency over UDP. Used in games, video streaming, and applications where UDP speed is needed with reliability.

name: DOTA2
title: Dota 2
description: Valve's popular multiplayer online battle arena game. Dota 2 uses Steam Datagram Relay for optimized multiplayer networking.

name: MUMBLE
title: Mumble
description: A free, open-source, low-latency voice chat application for gaming. Mumble is known for exceptional audio quality and very low latency.

name: YOJIMBO
title: Yojimbo Game Protocol
description: A secure client/server game networking library using UDP. Named after the Kurosawa film, it provides reliable connection-oriented communication for games.

name: ELECTRONICARTS
title: Electronic Arts
description: Game traffic from EA's titles — Apex Legends, FIFA, Madden, Battlefield, The Sims — and the EA App/Origin store.

name: STOMP
title: STOMP Messaging Protocol
description: Simple Text-Oriented Messaging Protocol — an interoperable protocol for asynchronous message passing. Clients using STOMP can communicate with message brokers like ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ.

name: RADMIN
title: Radmin
description: Radmin is a remote access software for Windows computers. Provides screen viewing, file transfer, and remote control.

name: RAFT
title: Raft Consensus Protocol
description: A consensus algorithm for distributed systems. Raft ensures that distributed databases or services agree on the same state even if some nodes fail.

name: CIP
title: Common Industrial Protocol
description: An application layer protocol for industrial automation used in EtherNet/IP, DeviceNet, and ControlNet networks. Standardized by ODVA for interoperability between industrial devices.

name: GEARMAN
title: Gearman Job Queue
description: A distributed job queue system. Applications submit jobs to Gearman and worker processes pick them up and execute them. Used for background processing.

name: TENCENTGAMES
title: Tencent Games
description: Traffic from Tencent's mobile and PC games — PUBG Mobile, Honor of Kings, and other Tencent game titles.

name: GAIJIN
title: Gaijin Entertainment
description: Game traffic from Gaijin games — primarily War Thunder (the realistic military vehicle game).

name: C1222
title: ANSI C12.22 Smart Metering
description: ANSI C12.22 protocol for communication with electric meters over IP networks. Used by utilities for smart meter reading and control.

name: HUAWEI
title: Huawei
description: Generic traffic from Huawei products and services — smartphones, network equipment, and cloud services.

name: HUAWEI_CLOUD
title: Huawei Mobile Cloud
description: Huawei's mobile cloud services for device backup, app sync, and cloud storage — used by Huawei and Honor smartphones.

name: DLEP
title: Dynamic Link Exchange Protocol
description: DLEP supports radio-aware IP routing by providing real-time metrics from radio modems to routers. Used in military and tactical communication networks.

name: BFD
title: Bidirectional Forwarding Detection
description: A lightweight protocol to quickly detect failures between two adjacent network nodes. BFD can detect link failures in milliseconds, faster than routing protocols.

name: NETEASE_GAMES
title: NetEase Games
description: Game traffic from NetEase — a major Chinese game company with titles like Knives Out, Rules of Survival, and co-publishing Minecraft in China.

name: PATHOFEXILE
title: Path of Exile
description: A free-to-play action RPG with deep mechanics and regular new content leagues. Developed by Grinding Gear Games.

name: GOOGLE_CALL
title: Google Voice/Video Call
description: Real-time audio/video call streams from Google services (primarily Google Meet). Separate from the signaling layer — this is the actual media stream.

name: PFCP
title: Packet Forwarding Control Protocol
description: Used in 5G/LTE networks to communicate between the control plane (SMF) and user plane (UPF). Part of the 3GPP service-based architecture for 5G networks.

name: FLUTE
title: FLUTE
description: File Delivery over Unidirectional Transport — designed for reliable one-to-many file distribution, such as satellite broadcasts or IPTV software updates.

name: LOLWILDRIFT
title: League of Legends: Wild Rift
description: Riot Games' mobile adaptation of League of Legends — a popular mobile MOBA for iOS and Android.

name: TESO
title: The Elder Scrolls Online
description: A massively multiplayer online RPG set in the Elder Scrolls universe (same world as Skyrim and Oblivion).

name: LDP
title: Label Distribution Protocol
description: Used in MPLS networks to establish label-switched paths. ISPs use LDP to set up fast forwarding paths through their networks.

name: KNXNET_IP
title: KNXnet/IP
description: KNX is a standard for building/home automation — controlling lights, blinds, HVAC, and security over IP. Very common in commercial building management systems.

name: BLUESKY
title: Bluesky
description: A decentralized social media platform built on the AT Protocol. Created by Twitter's original team as a federated alternative to centralized social networks.

name: MASTODON
title: Mastodon
description: Open-source decentralized social networking — anyone can run their own Mastodon server and users on different servers can still interact. Part of the Fediverse.

name: THREADS
title: Threads (Meta)
description: Meta's text-based social media platform, closely tied to Instagram. Launched as a Twitter/X competitor.

name: VIBER_VOIP
title: Viber Voice/Video Call
description: The real-time voice and video call streams within the Viber app — distinct from Viber's text messaging traffic.

name: ZUG
title: ZUG (Casper Blockchain)
description: ZUG is part of Casper 2.0 blockchain consensus protocol.

name: JRMI
title: Java RMI
description: Java Remote Method Invocation — allows Java objects to invoke methods on objects running in another JVM. Used in older Java enterprise applications.

name: RIPE_ATLAS
title: RIPE Atlas
description: RIPE NCC's global internet measurement platform. Small hardware probes around the world run network measurements. This is the traffic from those probes reporting results.

name: HLS
title: HTTP Live Streaming
description: Apple's adaptive streaming protocol. HLS splits video into small chunks and delivers them via HTTP. Apple TV, iOS, and most modern streaming platforms use HLS.

name: CLICKHOUSE
title: ClickHouse
description: An extremely fast open-source column-oriented database optimized for OLAP queries. Used by companies for real-time analytics on huge datasets.

name: NANO
title: Nano Cryptocurrency
description: A fast, feeless, and energy-efficient cryptocurrency using a block lattice data structure instead of a traditional blockchain.

name: OPENWIRE
title: OpenWire (ActiveMQ)
description: Apache ActiveMQ's native binary wire protocol. Used by Java applications to send and receive messages through ActiveMQ message broker.

name: CNP_IP
title: LonWorks over IP
description: Encapsulation of LonWorks (ISO 14908) building automation traffic over IP. LonWorks is used in building management systems for lighting, HVAC, and access control.

name: ATG
title: Automatic Tank Gauge
description: Protocol used by fuel storage tank monitoring systems to report fuel levels, temperature, and leak detection data.

name: TRDP
title: Train Real Time Data Protocol
description: IEC 61375 standardized protocol for data communication in trains — connecting different train subsystems (traction, brakes, doors) over IP.

name: LUSTRE
title: Lustre File System
description: A parallel distributed file system used in supercomputing. Lustre can scale to millions of files and petabytes of storage, used by many of the world's fastest supercomputers.

name: NORDVPN
title: NordVPN
description: One of the most popular commercial VPN services. NordVPN uses NordLynx (WireGuard-based) and OpenVPN protocols.

name: SURFSHARK
title: Surfshark VPN
description: A popular affordable VPN service offering unlimited simultaneous device connections.

name: CACTUSVPN
title: CactusVPN
description: A VPN service focused on streaming geo-unblocking and privacy.

name: WINDSCRIBE
title: Windscribe VPN
description: A Canadian VPN and ad-blocking service with a generous free tier.

name: SONOS
title: Sonos
description: Sonos smart speaker system traffic — music streaming to speakers, speaker group management, and the Sonos app communicating with speakers on your local network.

name: DINGTALK
title: DingTalk
description: Alibaba's enterprise collaboration platform — messaging, video calls, and business management tools. Very popular for business communication in China.

name: PALTALK
title: Paltalk
description: A video chat and group messaging application. Paltalk hosts large video chat rooms.

name: NAVER
title: Naver
description: South Korea's dominant search engine and internet portal, operating like Google in South Korea.

name: SHEIN
title: Shein
description: A Chinese fast-fashion retailer with a major global online presence.

name: TEMU
title: Temu
description: An online marketplace by PDD Holdings offering low-cost goods, rapidly growing globally.

name: TAOBAO
title: Taobao
description: Alibaba's massive Chinese online shopping platform — similar to eBay but much larger. One of the highest-traffic e-commerce sites in the world.

name: MIKROTIK
title: MikroTik MNDP
description: MikroTik Neighbor Discovery Protocol — allows MikroTik routers and switches to discover each other on a network for management and configuration.

name: DICOM
title: DICOM Medical Imaging
description: Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine — the standard for storing, transferring, and viewing medical images (X-rays, CT scans, MRIs) between hospital systems.

name: PARAMOUNTPLUS
title: Paramount+
description: ViacomCBS's streaming service with content from CBS, MTV, Comedy Central, Paramount Pictures, and Nickelodeon.

name: YANDEX_ALICE
title: Yandex Alice
description: Yandex's voice assistant (Russia's equivalent of Alexa). Traffic from smart speakers and apps using Alice for voice commands.

name: VIVOX
title: Vivox Voice Chat
description: A voice and text communication platform SDK used by game developers. Many popular games use Vivox for in-game voice chat (Fortnite, Valorant, PUBG).

name: DIGITALOCEAN
title: DigitalOcean
description: A cloud provider popular with developers and startups. Traffic hosted on DigitalOcean droplets (VMs) or other DigitalOcean services.

name: RUTUBE
title: Rutube
description: A Russian video hosting and streaming platform, similar to YouTube. Has grown in Russia following restrictions on Western platforms.

name: LAGOFAST
title: LagoFast Game Booster
description: A gaming VPN/acceleration service that routes game traffic through optimized paths to reduce lag and packet loss.

name: GEARUP_BOOSTER
title: GearUp Booster
description: A gaming performance optimization service that reduces latency by routing game traffic through better network paths.

name: RUMBLE
title: Rumble
description: A video sharing and live streaming platform known for hosting content from conservative creators and live streams.

name: UBIQUITY
title: Ubiquiti Services
description: Traffic from Ubiquiti network products communicating with Ubiquiti's cloud services and the UniFi management platform.

name: MSDO
title: Microsoft Delivery Optimization
description: Windows peer-to-peer download system for updates. Devices on the same network can share Windows Update packages with each other, reducing Microsoft's bandwidth and speeding up your updates.

name: ROCKSTAR_GAMES
title: Rockstar Games
description: Traffic from Rockstar Games' titles and launcher — GTA Online, Red Dead Online, and the Rockstar Games Launcher.

name: KICK
title: Kick.com
description: A live streaming platform that emerged as an alternative to Twitch with more lenient content policies.

name: HAMACHI
title: Hamachi VPN
description: LogMeIn's VPN service primarily used for creating virtual LAN networks between gaming friends or for simple remote access. Unlike anonymity VPNs, Hamachi is focused on virtual LAN creation.

name: GLBP
title: Gateway Load Balancing Protocol
description: Cisco's proprietary protocol that provides both router redundancy AND load balancing across multiple routers — more advanced than HSRP.

name: EASYWEATHER
title: EasyWeather Station Protocol
description: Proprietary UDP protocol used by certain weather stations to broadcast weather data over a local network.

name: MUDFISH
title: Mudfish Game VPN
description: A VPN service specialized for gaming — optimized to reduce ping and packet loss for online games rather than privacy.

name: TRISTATION
title: Triconex TriStation
description: Proprietary protocol for Schneider Electric's Triconex Safety Instrumented Systems — critical safety shutdown systems in oil/gas, nuclear, and chemical plants. Historically targeted by TRITON malware.
note: ⚠️ TriStation was targeted by TRITON/TRISIS malware — the first malware designed to attack safety systems. Isolate completely.

name: SAMSUNG_SDP
title: Samsung Service Discovery
description: Samsung's proprietary service discovery protocol used by Samsung TVs, soundbars, and smartphones to find and connect to each other on a local network.

name: MATTER
title: Matter Smart Home Protocol
description: The universal smart home standard backed by Apple, Google, Amazon, and Samsung. Matter lets devices from different brands (light bulbs, door locks, thermostats) all talk to each other using the same language, ending the fragmentation of smart home ecosystems. It runs over Wi-Fi and Thread (a low-power mesh network).

name: AWS_COGNITO
title: AWS Cognito (Auth Service)
description: Amazon's cloud-based user authentication service. When an app lets you sign in with email/password or social login (Google, Facebook), and that app is built on AWS, the authentication traffic often goes through Cognito. It handles user sign-up, sign-in, and access tokens.

name: AWS_API_GATEWAY
title: AWS API Gateway
description: Amazon's managed service for creating, publishing, and managing APIs. When you use a mobile app or website that calls its backend via AWS, traffic often routes through API Gateway. It acts as the 'front door' to backend services — you see URLs like execute-api.*.amazonaws.com.

name: AWS_KINESIS
title: AWS Kinesis (Data Streaming)
description: Amazon's real-time data streaming platform. Applications use Kinesis to continuously send large streams of data — like clickstream events, log data, or IoT sensor readings — to AWS for processing and analysis. Think of it as a high-speed data highway into the AWS cloud.

name: AWS_EC2
title: AWS EC2 (Virtual Servers)
description: Traffic going to or from Amazon EC2 virtual machines in the AWS cloud. EC2 is the core compute service of AWS — companies rent these virtual servers to run their websites, APIs, and applications. Seeing EC2 traffic means something on your network is talking to AWS-hosted server infrastructure.

name: AWS_EMR
title: AWS EMR (Big Data Processing)
description: Amazon Elastic MapReduce — a cloud service for processing massive datasets using frameworks like Apache Hadoop and Spark. Used by data engineers and analysts to crunch huge amounts of data without managing their own servers. EMR traffic usually indicates big data or analytics workloads.

name: AWS_S3
title: AWS S3 (Object Storage)
description: Amazon Simple Storage Service — one of the most widely used cloud services in the world. S3 stores files (objects) in 'buckets'. Apps use it to store profile photos, backups, video files, static website content, and more. If you download a file from almost any major app or website, there's a good chance it came from S3.

name: AWS_CLOUDFRONT
title: AWS CloudFront (Content Delivery Network)
description: Amazon's global CDN — a network of servers placed around the world to deliver content faster. When you load a website and assets (images, videos, scripts) come from *.cloudfront.net, they're being served by a CloudFront server physically close to you, reducing load times.

name: AWS_DYNAMODB
title: AWS DynamoDB (NoSQL Database)
description: Amazon's fully managed NoSQL database service. Apps that need to store and retrieve data at extreme scale (millions of requests per second) often use DynamoDB. Traffic to DynamoDB means an application is reading or writing to this managed database — common in serverless and mobile backends.

name: ESPN
title: ESPN Sports Streaming
description: Traffic from ESPN's digital platforms — the ESPN app, ESPN+, and ESPN.com. Includes live sports streaming (NFL, NBA, MLB, college sports), highlights, scores, and news. ESPN+ is a subscription streaming service for live events not on cable ESPN.

name: AKAMAI
title: Akamai CDN
description: One of the world's oldest and largest Content Delivery Networks. Akamai powers the delivery of content for major banks, governments, media companies, and software providers. Traffic from *.akamai.net or *.akamaihd.net means content is being served through Akamai's global edge network rather than directly from the origin company's servers.

name: JSON
title: JSON (Data Format over HTTP)
description: JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is the most common format for exchanging data between web apps and APIs. It's a lightweight, human-readable text format. nDPI detects JSON as a content type when apps communicate with APIs — seeing this in traffic means structured data is being sent (e.g., your app fetching your user profile or posting a form).

name: MSGPACK
title: MessagePack (Binary Serialization)
description: A compact binary version of JSON — it stores the same kind of structured data but takes up less space and transfers faster. Used by performance-sensitive apps and games that need to transfer lots of data efficiently. Less human-readable than JSON but much more efficient for machines.

name: GITHUB_COPILOT
title: GitHub Copilot (AI Coding)
description: GitHub's AI-powered coding assistant (built on OpenAI). When a developer uses Copilot in their code editor, it sends code context to GitHub's servers and receives AI-generated code suggestions back in real time. Traffic to copilot.github.com represents AI inference requests from developers.

name: GITHUB_PACKAGES
title: GitHub Packages (Package Registry)
description: GitHub's package hosting service. Developers publish and download software packages (npm, Docker images, Maven, NuGet) directly from GitHub. Traffic to pkg.github.com means a developer or CI/CD pipeline is publishing or downloading a software dependency through GitHub's registry.

name: GITHUB_ACTIONS
title: GitHub Actions (CI/CD Automation)
description: GitHub's built-in automation platform. When developers push code, GitHub Actions automatically runs tasks like tests, builds, and deployments. Traffic from GitHub Actions runners (the servers that execute these automated jobs) goes to pipelines.actions.githubusercontent.com and related services — common in developer-heavy environments.
